items.title: 68426_Nellie Lutcher oral history interview
items.q: Just like Elvis Presley, for instance. ... I'll use him

ctx.x: Repackaging them and I'm sure they wouldn't be doing it if there wasn't a market for it.

Well, there is a market. There's a market for anything that has ever happened one time, if it's been big and good. Just like Elvis Presley, for instance. Of course we're talking about years ahead of what we're talking about now, but I'll use him, and you know, there is a market.

Anybody who has ever made any -- got any recognition, earned any recognition, I think there's always a place for it, I really do. Because it means that there's something unique there, there's something different, and I think there's always a place for it. And I don't think that it's fair for record companies to do as they have done in the past, you know. Well, they can't make a million dollars off a record, so forget it, the record's pushed aside or put on the shelf someplace. And this is most unfair to the…
